source: Rulings 0139, 0140, 0142, 0143, 0144, 0145, 0146 and 0147 (Step 0 recursive set hierarchy, Level 0 root-set stress protocol, 17/17 self-describing charter Operation territory-stress protocols, E10 arc admission, A15/T3/SC0 foundational alignment, S17 source-comments rule and enforcer, S0 Level 2 medium sub-sets in SC1, and PC2 practice admission). Keyed before any reader ran and audited by a fresh B29 agent before prepare.

probes.question: How do layers, sets, and charters relate across the hierarchy of this corpus, and how is the root set of layers stressed under M12 to test whether a layer is missing, overlapping, or ready to retire?
probes.key: The corpus links four set structures across a recursive hierarchy: (1) the root set is the corpus itself, chartered by the root README.md and VISION.md, whose members are the layers (E2); (2) each knowledge layer is a child set voiced by its <prefix>0 charter at <directory>/README.md (E4) via delegation without inheritance; (3) sets/ (ST0) charters spanning sets that gather members across two or more layers without a directory of their own; and (4) a sub-population inside a layer whose rules differ from its parent's forms a nested sub-set (E3, such as S0 medium sub-sets). Under M12 and the root README.md, the root set of layers is stressed against VISION.md in three passes: a zero-home pass (sampling recurring concerns and backlog findings to see if any fits zero existing layers, testing spanning sets in sets/, nested sub-sets, or existing layers ahead of a second real occupant under A3 before proposing a layer), a two-home pass (testing adjacent layers against E2's altitude discriminator and neighbour questions), and a consumer and occupancy pass (verifying every layer has a consumer and flagging any single-occupant knowledge layer as a candidate for retirement so its next investigation either admits a second real member or folds the lone entry into a neighbour).
probes.rubric: 2 for both (a) the recursive hierarchy linking the root set of layers (README.md/VISION.md, E2), child layer sets (<prefix>0, E4), cross-layer spanning sets (sets/ ST0), and nested sub-sets (E3), and (b) how the root set of layers is stressed/evaluated (missing/zero-home vs spanning set/A3 two-occupant bar, two-home altitude test, and consumer/single-occupant retirement or fold-into-neighbour rule). 1 for one of the two halves, or for partial coverage (e.g., layer vs set and the README layer addition/retirement rules without the explicit root-set stress passes or full hierarchy). 0 otherwise.

probes.question: When running an M12 investigation on a set whose current population is small or lopsided - specifically components/ (C0), the explain set (ST1), and style/ (S0) - what does E4 require the charter's Operation section to state (and where do dated partitions and gaps live), and how does each of those three charters instruct an investigator to stress its territory against its Scope?
probes.key: E4 and M12 require a charter's Operation section to state how its territory is actively stressed against its Vision and Scope (the denominator, sampling pass, or generative test that exposes unpopulated regions of Scope, seam collisions, and bundled moves), while keeping dated partitions and discovered gaps in docs/investigations/. Specifically: (1) C0 (components/README.md) stresses its territory when few anchored cores are recorded by composing registered components across orthogonal reference architectures, testing for recurring boxes at architecture altitude with no registered component across two or more architectures, contract mismatches/glue across consumes or contains edges, and component duties requiring an 'and' conjunction at box altitude; (2) ST1 (sets/ST1-explain.md) walks the full human-exchange arc (initial framing, status/bad-news delivery, teaching, K5 survey, M10 guided dialogue, AR3 board selection, and decision ratification), tests the boundary tensions under Boundaries (K5, AR3, RU1), and isolates individual moves via single-move paired human comparisons rather than package rewrites; and (3) S0 (style/README.md) crosses its four claimed media (documents, messages to a human, commit messages, code names and comments) against artifact grains, samples real artifacts in each cell for recurring defects, checks whether a second non-document rule triggers a medium sub-set, and tests rules held by reading for deterministic predicates a script in tools/ could hold.
probes.rubric: 2 for stating E4/M12's Operation territory-stress requirement plus the specific territory-stress passes for all three charters (C0 reference-architecture synthesis/seams/conjunction test, ST1 exchange-arc walk/boundary tensions/single-move isolation, and S0 four-media-by-grain sampling/sub-set trigger/predicate test); noting that dated partitions and gaps stay in docs/investigations/ is consistent with full marks and not required on its own to avoid a cap. 1 for the general E4/M12 rule plus partial or pre-0140 Operation descriptions (e.g., naming C0's union of anchored cores, ST1's moment partitioning, and S0's non-overlap/predicate check without the active stress passes). 0 otherwise.

probes.question: How does practices/ (PC0) stress its territory across the moments of a unit of work, how does it filter candidates that belong in methods/ (M0), style/ (S0), or rules/ (RU0), what is required for a remaining candidate to earn admission, and what happens if no second practice earns admission?
probes.key: Under PC0 (practices/README.md) and M0's placement order (axiom, procedure, style, rule, practice), an M12 analysis stresses practices/ across the moments of a unit of work (entering, committing to a design, verifying, deciding what to keep, treating the record, and handing over) by auditing candidate habits in the project's standing context (SC2 / AGENTS.md) and recurring judgement failures in its decision records (AR4 / docs/DECISIONS.md) and backlog (AR5 / docs/BACKLOG.md). It filters out any candidate that produces a result of its own (routed to methods/), governs artifact form (routed to style/), or leaves a verifiable trace in the record that a tool or reader can check (routed to rules/, including any existing practice that acquires a trace). For remaining trace-free candidates, admission under M13 requires observed evidence that following the practice changes the work (a practice is never minted merely to fill a gap); if or while the layer holds a single member, failure to admit a second practice leaves practices/ a candidate for retirement under the root charter (or its lone entry is folded into a neighbour).
probes.rubric: 2 for (a) stressing across the moments of work by auditing standing-context/DECISIONS/BACKLOG candidates, (b) the M0 placement filter routing result-producing steps to methods/, form to style/, and trace-leaving obligations to rules/ (plus the observed-evidence admission requirement for remaining trace-free candidates rather than minting to fill a gap), and (c) noting that if or while the layer holds a single member, failure to admit a second practice leaves practices/ a candidate for retirement under the root charter or folds its lone entry into a neighbour (whether or not a second practice such as PC2 has since been admitted). 1 for the M0 placement filter and observed-evidence admission rule without the moments/standing-context stress pass or single-occupant retirement consequence. 0 otherwise.

probes.question: In the foundational layers, (a) what is an arc in this corpus, which entity defines it, and what are its two representations across layers; (b) why is there no solo-agent trait complementing T3 multi-agent; and (c) how does A15 Recursive Elevation's human-gate filter divide decisions by altitude against E1 and A13?
probes.key: (a) E10 (entities/E10-arc.md) defines an arc as a bounded, multi-step initiative that advances a system from its current state toward a declared target across gated steps, steered as one whole and closed only when terminal proof is reconciled across the steps that compose it. It appears in two layer-specific representations: as a staged value-chain tree of rungs climbing a fixed summit with lifecycle states, dependency edges, and anti-amnesia revival triggers (K6, K16, usable with or without a coordination substrate), and as a coordination-substrate execution graph of work items and gates seeded from a blueprint on E9, operated under a driver lease, and closed by a proof-level closeout packet (W17-W19, W21, K18, K23-K26). (b) Under T3 (traits/T3-multi-agent.md) and T0, multi-agent's complement is not a trait because in an organisation of one, the obligation to check one's own work by means the author's reasoning cannot bias binds every system on the any-system floor (A16), and when a gate requires an independent agent and none exists, the gate waits or the director decides it (W0 constraints 2 and 9, R0); neither obligation needs a solo-agent trait. (c) Under A15 (axioms/A15-recursive-elevation.md), E1, and A13, collaborating agents filter questions by altitude: technical or operational questions below the director's altitude that held evidence, source truth, or standing charter invariants settle are decided by the agents, recorded in an append-only decision record, and surfaced in the operational log where the director may re-aim charter intent or reclaim any choice that crossed into the director's altitude; genuine authority calls (charter intent or trade-offs, ratification, access or production rights, external commitments, or budget) belong to the director alone, are never pre-decided by agents, and arrive pre-staged with the full, unbiased option set and a labeled recommendation (using a revealed-preference lean only on a genuine inter-axiom divergence, with no pre-selected or auto-enacted default ahead of ratification, A13).
probes.rubric: 2 for all three parts: (a) E10 defining arc and distinguishing its value-chain rung-tree (K6/K16) and coordination-substrate blueprint-graph (E9, W17-W19/W21, K18/K23-K26) representations, (b) T3's solo-agent complement resolved without a trait because A16 binds on the floor and W0/R0 govern gate waiting or director ratification, and (c) A15's human-gate filter separating agent-settleable technical/operational questions below the director's altitude (E1) from director authority calls presented with the full, unbiased option set and a labeled recommendation (A13, never pre-decided). 1 for one or two of the three parts, or for pre-0143 readings (e.g., arc undefined in entities/, T3 saying its complement is not a trait yet, or A15 saying all escalations arrive pre-decided without the E1/A13 authority split). 0 otherwise.

probes.question: When running an M12 investigation on the foundational layers - entities/ (E0), traits/ (T0), axioms/ (A0), and schemas/ (SC0) - how does each charter's Operation section instruct an investigator to stress its territory against its Vision and Scope?
probes.key: Under E4 and M12, each foundational charter's Operation section states an active territory-stress pass alongside recording dated partitions and gaps in the project's record (docs/investigations/) and backlog (AR5): (1) E0 (entities/README.md) partitions defined entities across the five subjects the corpus leans on (authority, corpus structure, what is engineered, work and its proof, and coordination), scans across knowledge layers for recurring nouns leaned on across two or more layers without an entity entry or with divergent local definitions, and applies the two-readers test to each candidate (while routing single-layer member terms to their charter, how-to procedures to methods/ or skills/, and instance shapes to schemas/); (2) T0 (traits/README.md) partitions traits by the architectural question each settles (state and how behaviour is specified, who acts and who is in the loop, and what reasons on the critical path), tests every axiom's applies-to tags for floor exclusivity (any-system never combined with a trait) and for traits named by only one axiom or none, and tests each trait's absence complement against the axioms, roles, and work-types; (3) A0 (axioms/README.md) partitions axioms across the six failure classes they forbid (truth of state and claims, boundaries and promotion, operation and recovery, cognition and context, authority, and knowledge, learning, and elevation), tests adjacent pairs for restatement or boundary tension, verifies that every applies-to tag obeys the floor and trait rules in T0, and samples real system failures and backlog (AR5) findings for drift modes no current axiom forbids; and (4) SC0 (schemas/README.md) inventories every frontmatter block, lifecycle document type in artifacts/, JSON or YAML configuration or manifest file, and resource envelope across the project, and cross-checks each against the contracts in catalog.json, the validators in tools/, and the paired contract tests in schemas/tests/ to surface any ungoverned structured artifact, unmapped resource kind, or hand-rolled duplicate check.
probes.rubric: 2 for stating the specific Operation territory-stress passes across all four foundational charters: E0 (five-subject partition, cross-layer recurring-noun scan for missing/divergent definitions, and two-readers test), T0 (architectural-question partition, applies-to any-system floor exclusivity + zero/single-axiom check, and absence-complement test across axioms/roles/work-types), A0 (six-failure-class partition, pairwise restatement/boundary tension check, T0 applies-to check, and unforbidden failure/backlog sampling), and SC0 (project-wide structured-file inventory across frontmatter, artifacts/ lifecycle types, JSON/YAML configs/manifests, and resource envelopes cross-checked against catalog.json contracts, tools/ validators, and schemas/tests/ contract tests). 1 for partial coverage (e.g., naming two or three of the four stress passes, or giving pre-0142 Operation summaries such as E0 one-home/cited/two-readers, T0 non-overlap/absence, A0 orthogonality/neighbour routing, and SC0 non-overlap/check/consumer/catalog.json confirmation without the active territory-stress passes). 0 otherwise.

probes.question: In the style/ (S0) and practices/ (PC0) sets: (a) how does S0 partition its members into sub-sets and which frontmatter field in SC1 holds that partition; (b) which style rule governs comments in executable scripts and source files, what tool enforces it, and what four properties does that tool check; and (c) what is the second practice in practices/ alongside PC1, what does it require when inspecting evaluation or test results, and why is it a practice rather than a rule?
probes.key: (a) Under S0 (style/README.md, Sub-sets and Index) and SC1 (schemas/catalog-entry/v1alpha1/catalog-entry.schema.json), style/ partitions its members into four medium sub-sets - documents, messages, commits, and code - declared once per member in the required medium frontmatter field (forbidden on S0 and non-style entries) and grouped under ### Sub-set: <medium> headings in style/README.md's generated Index. (b) S17 (style/S17-source-comments-state-duty-and-why.md), enforced by tools/s17-source-comments.sh, governs comments in executable scripts and source files; its tool checks four properties on executable scripts in tools/*.sh and tools/*.mjs: (1) line 2 matches (#|//) (<stem>|<filename>) - <one-line summary>, (2) the opening comment block declares Sovereign duty: (on non-test scripts) and Usage: (on all scripts), (3) comment lines contain only printable ASCII (0x20-0x7E and tab), and (4) comment lines contain no commented-out shell or JavaScript statements (unless exempted by a style-check: allow S17 marker). (c) PC2 (practices/PC2-check-the-splits-that-favour-you.md) requires inspecting the cells and splits that favour your change (such as 2 of 2 head gains, passing gates, or concordant readings) with the same scrutiny as failing ones - auditing favourable splits back to raw answers/reasons, verifying that passing guard/mutant probes actually landed, and questioning self-corroboration. It is a practice in practices/ rather than a rule in rules/ because when a favourable cell is inspected and turns out to be sound, nothing in the finished artifact afterwards leaves a trace showing that the favourable split was re-read.
probes.rubric: 2 for all three parts: (a) S0's four medium sub-sets (documents, messages, commits, code) declared via SC1's medium frontmatter field (noting their grouping in style/README.md's generated Index is consistent with full marks and not required on its own), (b) S17 and tools/s17-source-comments.sh with its four checked properties (line-2 <name> - <summary> header, Sovereign duty: on non-test scripts and Usage: in the opening block, printable ASCII only in comments, and no commented-out code statements), and (c) PC2 (check the splits that favour you) requiring equal scrutiny on favourable/passing cells and explaining that it is a practice rather than a rule because re-reading a sound favourable split leaves no trace in the finished artifact. 1 for one or two of the three parts, or for pre-Wave-2 answers (e.g., S0 holding a flat index with only S15 as a single non-document rule, S8 covering only markdown code blocks with no source-comment rule, or PC1 as the sole practice in practices/). 0 otherwise.
